title: Grand Design Spiral Arms in the Compact, Embedded Protoplanetary Disk of Haro 6-13
question: Does the compact Haro 6-13 disk host millimeter continuum spiral arms at ~5 au resolution, and what could form them (gravitational instability, infall, companions, flybys)?

recipe.goal: Self-calibrate, combine and image the continuum
recipe.method: Align EBs on disk center, self-calibrate short-baseline EBs, align and combine with long-baseline data, self-calibrate again and image with multiscale CLEAN at robust 0.5, then apply primary beam correction
key_parameters: robust = 0.5
Long-baseline data: 1 phase round with a solution interval spanning the observation before combining

recipe.goal: Image CO isotopologue cubes and moment maps
recipe.method: uvcontsub, multiscale CLEAN with auto-multithresh, primary beam correction, integrated intensity and intensity-weighted velocity maps, spectra from circular apertures
key_parameters: Velocity resolution 0.65 km/s (12CO), 1.35 km/s (13CO, C18O)
robust 0.5 with 0.3 arcsec uv-taper
Integration ranges 0.2-10.6 km/s (12CO) and 2.75-8.15 km/s (13CO, C18O) in LSRK, negative pixels clipped
Velocity maps use a 4 sigma clip
C18O spectrum aperture radius 1.5 arcsec

recipe.goal: Unsharp-mask image and azimuthally averaged radial profile
recipe.method: Unsharp masking for visual enhancement; deprojected radial intensity profile from the original CLEAN image
key_parameters: scale factor 2, Gaussian filter sigma 0.06 arcsec

recipe.method: Per-SPW correction of absolute weight scaling with visread
key_parameters: weights downscaled by factors from ~1 to ~5

recipe.method: protomidpy fits the 1D radial intensity profile as a Fourier-Bessel series, with disk P.A., inclination and offsets, directly to the visibilities
key_parameters: Flat priors: cos i [0,1]; P.A. [0,180] deg; dx, dy [-0.1,0.1] arcsec; gamma [0.01,0.15] arcsec; log alpha [-4,5]
24 walkers, 15000 steps, first 1000 steps discarded as burn-in
assumptions: Disk is axisymmetric and geometrically thin

recipe.goal: CLEAN the model and the residual visibilities
recipe.method: CLEAN the maximum a posteriori model visibilities like the data, then CLEAN residual visibilities (observed minus model) with a uv taper
key_parameters: residual image uv taper 0.02 arcsec; synthesized beam 0.046 x 0.030 arcsec (15.9 deg)

recipe.method: filfinder run on the protomidpy residual image; coordinates converted to disk R and theta
key_parameters: smoothing size 2 pixels (0.006 arcsec); intensity threshold 0.03 mJy/beam
adaptive-threshold mask width 4 pixels (0.012 arcsec, ~1.5 au)
size threshold 300 au^2; minimum length 3 synthesized beams
assumptions: For S2, points with R < 10 au not used because they belong to the central bar-like residual

recipe.goal: Fit Archimedean spirals with Gaussian-process regression and derive pitch angles
recipe.method: Each arm fit independently with R(theta)=a-b*theta, GP regression (white noise + squared exponential kernel) in log parameter space; pitch angle from tan(beta)=|d ln R/d theta|
key_parameters: Priors for both arms: ln b [1,3], ln sigma^2 [-5,5], ln A [-4,4], ln C [-10,0]
30 walkers, 5,000 burn-in steps plus 10,000 steps per arm; median and 68% interval reported
assumptions: Adjacent pixels correlated because the beam is oversampled, modeled via GP kernel

recipe.method: Extract intensities from the original CLEAN image along the best-fit spirals and divide by an interpolated background of per-1-au-bin minimum disk intensity
key_parameters: radial bins of 1 au for the background
assumptions: Uncertainty on arm and background intensity equals the image rms

recipe.goal: Measure continuum flux and disk-averaged spectral index
recipe.method: Flux within a 1 arcsec radius circle at 229.5 GHz combined with literature 97.5 GHz flux; alpha computed from the two fluxes
key_parameters: 10% systematic flux calibration uncertainty dominates
assumptions: Disk-averaged index only; 3 mm data only marginally resolve the disk

recipe.goal: Compare brightness temperature with dust temperature
recipe.method: Analytic passively irradiated disk dust temperature compared with observed brightness temperature from the CLEAN image, with and without scattering (chi = 0.6)
key_parameters: flaring angle 0.02; L* = 0.79 Lsun
scattering case chi = I_nu/B_nu = 0.6 for DSHARP composition
assumptions: Dust temperature set by passive irradiation; the estimate is crude

recipe.goal: Estimate Toomre Q from optically thick dust surface density
recipe.method: Sigma_dust = tau/kappa_abs with tau = -cos i ln(1 - I/B(Td)); Q = c_s Omega_K/(pi G Sigma) with gas-to-dust 100; Td = max(observed brightness temperature, analytic Td)
key_parameters: tau estimated only for R > 5 au; tau = 4 set where brightness temperature exceeds dust temperature in the inner disk
kappa_abs = 0.4, 1.9, 1.0 cm2/g for a_max = 0.1, 1, 10 mm, n(a) ~ a^-3.5
assumptions: mean molecular weight 2.37; gas-to-dust ratio 100; M* = 0.91 Msun; absorption-only opacity

recipe.goal: Estimate disk mass from C18O flux
recipe.method: C18O flux within a 1 arcsec radius circle mapped to a maximum disk mass using a thermochemical model grid
